\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بڑھاپا} (buṛhāpā)}{بڑھاپا (buṛhāpā)}]{\ur{بڑھاپا} (buṛhāpā) — old age}

\label{lesson:UR-C492-burhapa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a divorce, then the Urdu for to forgive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بڑھاپا}}
\textbf{\ur{بڑھاپا}} — \emph{buṛhāpā} — \textquotedblleft{}old age\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بڑھاپے} \ur{میں} \ur{نیند} \ur{کم} \ur{ہو} \ur{جاتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{buṛhāpe meṅ nīṅd kam ho jātī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In old age people sleep less.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بڑھاپا}} (\emph{buṛhāpā}) is inherited: it is built on \textbf{\ur{بوڑھا}}, \textquotedblleft{}old\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{buḍḍha}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 9271), with the abstract ending \emph{-āpā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buṛhāpā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buṛhāpā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buṛhāpe meṅ nīṅd kam ho jātī hai.} — In old age people sleep less.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a divorce, then the Urdu for to forgive, then say \emph{buṛhāpā} again
\end{itemize}
